prize_parts.citation: For the development of reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry on clustered surfaces, which made massively parallel DNA sequencing possible.

statement.case_for: I keep B011 with Balasubramanian and Klenerman after reading the full exchange. The case is still the one I apply to every candidate: something completely new that has already changed what scientists can do. Reversible 3'-blocked fluorescent nucleotides, cleavable dyes, clustered surfaces and single-molecule-sensitive detection are molecular design problems that were solved with chemistry, and the result is two decades of universal use across genetics, cancer, infectious disease and, as Chabes points out, mutation and replication-error research. Round 1 sharpened the attribution rather than weakening it. Only Linke supported the narrow reading, but nobody has shown that the two-name lineage is wrong; the objections concern Rothberg, Mayer and Ju, who are excluded by a deliberate choice of one chemical lineage and not by oversight. A citation on reversible-terminator chemistry says exactly what the chemistry was, and it carries no maturity risk, which cannot be said for the leading alternatives.
statement.case_against: The objection I take most seriously is the one raised by six colleagues from different angles: that the credit does not map to one clean discovery and that the prize could read as a technology award. Rothberg's 454 platform was first to market, Ju's terminator work and Mayer's clustering idea have real claims, and a committee that cannot defend the exclusion of any of them should not award this prize. Zou's and Somfai's point that the size of downstream impact is not the same as a chemical discovery is fair, and the expert report on the sequencing field should settle which lineage is the chemical core. I also accept that B011 has only two explicit supporters at most and that a majority of five is unreachable unless B010 supporters or others can accept it. B010 has broader support and no one disputes its science.

responses.point: Linke ranks B046 first and accepts that B011 is the no-maturity-risk option, but would support it only as the two-person Balasubramanian-Klenerman prize for reversible-terminator chemistry and would not add Rothberg without a clear argument.
responses.response: We are now aligned on the configuration and I thank you for stating the condition so plainly: one lineage, two names, and a citation that names the chemistry. On B046 my reservation stands. Your own uncertainty is that which in-cell condensates are equilibrium phase-separated and functionally essential is open, and the prize would then rest on the in vitro thermodynamics. I find that a weaker claim of changed practice than a method used daily in every sequencing laboratory, and the third name (Rosen, Pappu or Mittag) is not settled either.

responses.point: Aili argues that B010 has cleaner conceptual authorship and more central chemistry than B011, and that demanding fully settled clinical proof would have delayed earlier prizes.
responses.response: This is the argument that moved me most, and I accept the comparison with earlier prizes. The cereblon mechanism for thalidomide-class drugs, with glue-class medicines already in patients, is a real consequence and not a promise. Where I still differ is in what the two prizes would cite. Crews-Deshaies-Handa leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray, and whether PROTACs and glues are one discovery or two is not yet settled, whereas the Solexa citation has one clear object. I therefore keep B010 as my first alternative and would vote for it if B011 cannot gather support.

responses.point: Chabes argues that quantitative mechanism and glue-class medicines outweigh the absence of an approved PROTAC, and that B028 is not an independent route to a sequencing prize because it overlaps with B011.
responses.response: I agree on B028 and have dropped nanopores from my thinking as an independent route, since a sequencing prize can be given once. On B010 I concede that the lack of an approved heterobifunctional degrader should not alone disqualify it. My concern is the one you describe yourself, that a combined PROTAC and glue citation risks looking stitched together. If the committee can write one sentence on induced proximity that is honest about both strands and about the third name (Handa or Ciulli), I would find it hard to object.

responses.point: Somfai backs B035 on clean attribution (Buchwald and Hartwig), calls B011 a prize that might read as technology, and would support B011 only if a defensible trio can be agreed.
responses.response: You answered my round-1 question about 2010 as well as it can be answered: C-N coupling needed its own ligand design and mechanistic work, and I now place B035 as my second alternative, since it fits the simple, general-method prize I admire. On B011 I do not think a trio is required. The defensible configuration is two names, and I would say that Rothberg's pyrosequencing is a different lineage that a Solexa-focused citation leaves open without misrepresentation, in the same way that you would handle Kosugi.

responses.point: Zou argues that the size of downstream effect is not the same as chemical discovery and that the structure-directing agent in zeolites is a sharper chemical object than a sequencing platform.
responses.response: I accept the distinction, and it is why I restrict the citation to the nucleotide chemistry and surface method and not to the sequencers. I do not agree that B002 has the sharper claim: the credit boundary with Yu and Tsapatsis is open, you have a possible conflict that you asked the committee to judge, and the committee has just recognised porous materials in 2025 with MOFs, so the timing concern you raise yourself cuts against it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a two-name Solexa lineage prize without Rothberg, Mayer or Ju, and what the expert report on sequencing says about which lineage is the chemical core.
Whether sequencing-by-synthesis is judged chemistry-led enough for the Chemistry prize rather than Medicine or Physiology.
Whether B010 can be given one honest citation covering PROTACs and cereblon glues, and whether Handa or Ciulli is the right third name.
Whether I should move to B010 in the vote if B011 cannot reach five votes.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal is needed for B011, B010 or B035. My background in biomolecular simulation is scientifically close to B038 (Car-Parrinello), and I have no personal or institutional tie to Car or Parrinello; B038 is no longer among my alternatives. I have no tie to any credited name on the shortlist.
